steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: The Imamate is a Shi'a Muslim belief that Allah appointed twelve Imams to lead the Muslim community after Muhammad's death. These Imams are divinely chosen, infallible and have special spiritual authority. This is one of the Five Roots of Usul ad-Din in Shi'a Islam. | Exam Tip: The Imamate is the key difference between Sunni and Shi'a Islam. Sunni Muslims believe caliphs should be chosen by the community; Shi'a Muslims believe Allah appointed the Imams. This is why the two traditions have different approaches to authority, law and leadership. | RS Exam Tips — The Imamate: 1.
